name: Semiconductors (SMH/SOX)
summary: Semiconductors / the AI complex, Day 241. The non-war shock now dominates Asian equity flows and has become a credit story. The chip index fell nearly 12% in the fortnight to 23 Oct — an eight-session losing streak (the longest since 2008), a KOSPI circuit breaker on 15 Oct, and on 22 Oct a 6.7% drop when Meta reported its first negative free cash flow in over a decade as capex outran operating cash. CoreWeave's bonds yield above 15% and its stock is down 30%; Meta's default-swap spread hit a record. Fundamentals at the fabs are strong (TSMC beat and guided Q4 up 14%; Samsung's preliminary operating profit ~₩107trn), so the selloff is about who pays for the AI build-out, not chip demand. The market link to the war is mostly through the Fed (hot CPI); the link to India is that money leaving Korea and US tech did not come to India. Tests this week: whether Microsoft, Alphabet or Amazon also show capex above operating cash flow (28–29 Oct), and SK hynix/Samsung guidance.

recent_signals.headline: SMH -2.2% Friday, -9.7% on the month, +20.0% still on three months — the AI complex is de-rating from an extreme, not collapsing. The bear case is fully non-Iranian (DRAM litigation, CXMT, Kimi K3, ASML-TSMC pricing) with one genuine war leg: helium. **The timing point that matters: helium rationing that began in March/April shows up in wafer starts within 1-2 weeks but in SHIPMENTS on an 8-12 WEEK LAG — i.e. it lands now, July-September.** Korea is 64.7% Qatar-dependent for helium and Taiwan ~69% GCC-dependent, against ~30-35% of global supply offline for 3-5 years. No formal production cut has been announced by Samsung, SK Hynix or TSMC. Watch for the unusual configuration of a SUPPLY-constrained memory market inside a DEMAND downturn. CONFIRMED.
